name: Tinted amber glass slab desk

reasons: Single three-quarter view: rear long side of the top, the slab underside, the outer face of the far (+X) panel and both floor contacts are unseen; all are recovered by the object's left-right symmetry.
Silhouette is three unambiguous plates (one horizontal, two vertical X-normal), so macro geometry is safe.
Body-tinted transparent glass: photographed colour is the sum of overlapping thicknesses, so albedo and the vertical tint gradient are approximated procedurally.
L-brackets are small in frame (~0.10 m arms) and read through glass; arm length ±0.02 m and screw count per arm are approximated.
Presence of concealed glides at the floor line cannot be confirmed; flat glass-to-floor contact assumed.

materials.subtype: amber body-tinted float glass, 0.012 m thick, transmissive with warm absorption (ior 1.52)
dark bronze / oil-rubbed brass flat bar stock

mustMatch: Top slab is 1.400 m wide × 0.700 m deep × 0.012 m thick, its upper face at 0.740 m; no frame, apron or stretcher anywhere.

Both end panels are 0.012 m thick, 0.640 m deep and 0.728 m tall, standing X-normal with bottom edges flat on the floor (y=0); footprint is two parallel 0.64 m lines whose outer faces are 1.340 m apart.
Panels are set inboard 0.030 m from each slab end and 0.030 m from the slab front and rear edges, so the slab overhangs on all four sides.

Four dark bronze L-brackets, two per panel on the inner face, centres 0.550 m apart in depth; each has a 0.110 m vertical arm hanging from the slab underside and a 0.090 m horizontal arm reaching inboard, bar width 0.035 m and thickness 0.004 m.
Two Ø0.008 m screw heads per bracket arm, 0.040 m apart (four per bracket).
All exposed edges are flat-polished arrises 0.012 m wide with a 0.002 m eased corner — no chamfered bullnose, no metal trim.
niceToHave: Vertical transmitted-tint gradient on the panels: warmer #B3652F in the top 0.15 m to #7A3617 in the lowest 0.24 m.
Two pale maker decals 0.020 × 0.015 m, 0.140 m apart, 0.05 m above the floor on the outer face of the near panel only.
Deeper amber where the two glass thicknesses overlap in view (panel seen through the slab edge).
Soft broad specular sheet crossing the slab from its front-left corner toward the centre.
Faint contact shadow under each panel bottom edge.
